openItems.topic: Measurement device conditions and support baseline
openItems.known: Four devices report webview rendering, callable wx.getPerformance, registered observers and the same six runtime-supported types. After the snapshot-source correction was requested, OPPO returned 10 rows, down from 20; the previous visible repeated type/duration patterns are absent. Six rows display durations (appLaunch 1532ms, firstRender 701ms, evaluateScript 4ms, plus redacted render/interaction values); route and the three paint/content timing points have no duration. The OPPO report does not embed its probe revision. A new SEA-AL10 report shows WeChat 8.0.79/base library 3.17.5 (earlier report was 3.17.4); the user confirmed Android GPU Rendering bars appeared over the WeChat probe and refreshed while scrolling. ADB confirms the connected device is SEA-AL10/Android 10/API 29 and foreground AppBrandUI00 during capture. SurfaceFlinger returned an attributable host layer but its first capture spanned about 33 seconds and was not synchronized to scrolling. A separate read-only gfxinfo query against com.tencent.mm:appbrand0 returned a ViewRoot matching AppBrandUI00; the main WeChat process was excluded because its ViewRoot was LauncherUI. Before reset, the process showed 3033 cumulative frames and 13 janky frames. The first reset exited 0 and its stats-since timestamp changed; a post-reset query restarted at 66 frames. A later unsynchronized read showed 301 frames/0 janky. A second reset before the requested gesture changed the stats-since timestamp and verified zero frames immediately afterward. The first post-scroll dump showed 1636 aggregate frames/0 janky across about 240.6 seconds and no input timestamps. A later 15.226-second live poll overlapped a user-confirmed approximate five-second scroll: the count stayed at 0 through 5.331 seconds, then rose to 203 frames with 1 janky frame (0.49%). The gesture start/end were not logged, and all ten final rows had NewestInputEvent=0 and the no-event OldestInputEvent sentinel. A later guarded synthetic swipe on the visible AppBrandUI00 host returned 93 frames/0 janky over 5.419 seconds of host command time, but its ten recent rows had no input timestamps and the WebView compositor was not isolated. This is feasibility data only, not a scroll FPS or QP05 result. No frame-rate item was found in the IDE Tools menu; System Tracing was not found under Debugging on the backup Huawei. A later 20-second manual FrameTimeline-only capture on OPPO PLJ110 overlapped the user-reported approximate five-second scroll: 538 actual and 538 expected frames appeared on the named AppBrand host layer over 10.079 seconds, all classified on-time with no jank type. The 317.55ms maximum adjacent gap has no timestamped gesture bounds, and no independent WebView frame stream was found; this is method evidence only.

openItems.localTraceEvidence: A seven-second atrace overlapped a five-second synthetic swipe and retained 61,017/61,017 events. Input, AppBrand doFrame and SurfaceFlinger vsync markers were present, but no separately attributable WebView presented-frame stream was found. Perfetto's traced service disconnected and a larger atrace buffer failed; a 1,024 KB buffer succeeded. This is measurement-method feasibility only.
openItems.oppoFrameTimelineEvidence: Historical 60Hz capture: 152 host frames over 2.845 seconds, 1,204 input-delivery slices, 789 doFrame slices, 948 systrace import failures, and a 329.57ms maximum adjacent gap; not gesture-correlated. On 2026-11-01, the first manual FrameTimeline-only capture window was missed (9 actual-frame records: 3 named status-bar, 6 unnamed, 0 AppBrand); the Trace Processor error-stat query had no nonzero rows. An 8-second FrameTimeline-only trace overlapping a 5-second ADB synthetic swipe recorded 94 actual-frame records, including 45 named AppBrand host frames over 1.034 seconds and a 329.87ms maximum adjacent host-frame gap; the status bar had 2 frames over 1.004 seconds. A later 20-second FrameTimeline-only capture overlapped a user-reported approximate five-second manual scroll and recorded 538 actual and 538 expected frames on the named AppBrand host layer over 10.079 seconds; all actual records were On-time Present with jank type None, and the maximum adjacent host-frame gap was 317.55ms. Gesture boundaries were not timestamped, no input tracks were included, and the embedded WebView was not isolated, so this is method-feasibility evidence only—not a scroll FPS, app-stall attribution, product-page result or QP05 evidence.

The user must review/accept the Android SDK license and install those exact SDK packages before the local build can continue. Installation requires a separate confirmation. VPN consent, update-source packaging behavior and tool evidence are in docs/sp01-weak-network-tool-review-20261031.md. On 2026-11-01 the user said the router owner is temporarily unavailable to ask, so no firmware, management-access or configuration-consent evidence is available. A third-party firmware project does not prove this device runs OpenWrt. The large packet-loss variation prevents freezing a stable normal network profile. SDK licenses were accepted by the user on 2026-11-02, and build-tools;35.0.0 plus platforms;android-36 are installed. The isolated :app:assembleKernelDebug build succeeded on Temurin 17.0.20.1+1. A corrected debug APK passed offline package and signature checks; permissions are recorded in latestBuildEvidence. At the build-record stage, no installation, VPN activation, or weak-network injection had been performed; the later device installation is recorded in deviceInstallEvidence. Three user-pasted 30-call rounds per normal and light-weak labels are now recorded on Huawei SEA-AL10; all 180 calls succeeded. The two new adjacent rerun pairs show light-label averaged-middle P50 increases of 82ms and 108.5ms, but P95 direction is inconsistent across the three rounds (first round normal is higher; later reruns are higher under the light label). The three-run average of per-run P50 is 288.5ms normal vs 381.83ms light; the average P95 is 581.67ms normal vs 545.33ms light. Results are consistent with a median application-roundtrip increase but do not establish Pakomo VPN state or configured impairment enforcement. The probe does not measure link RTT, throughput, jitter or packet loss. The user-pasted reruns did not include per-run timestamps, diagnostic counters, or VPN state/recovery confirmation. A later agent-operated correlated run on Huawei SEA-AL10 confirmed Pakomo light forwarding before the sample; status before stop showed activeFlows=4, delayed=93, dropped=0. The same 30-call read-only CloudBase sample succeeded 30/30 (lower-middle P50=403ms, nearest-rank P95=622ms, max=6407ms). Pakomo stop was confirmed and validated Wi-Fi returned as NOT_VPN within the fresh 60-second authorization. Aggregate counters cannot identify individual CloudBase calls, so this confirms a bounded correlated run but not per-request shaping or exact impairment enforcement. A later one-shot agent-operated Pakomo light run produced 30/30 successful read-only CloudBase application round trips (P50=398ms, P95=656ms, max=1985ms). Pakomo was stopped and Wi-Fi was connected with no VPN network agent found; internet reachability was not independently validated. The device timer showed 68 seconds against a 60-second authorization, exceeding it by 8 seconds. This run is diagnostic-only and not eligible for R04 acceptance; it does not prove per-call shaping or exact configured impairment values. A later bounded run on 2026-11-02 confirmed Pakomo start returned forwarding/active with application scope and appliedRule=light; the SP01 network sampling page completed 30 read-only calls, and stop returned stopped/active=false. The start-to-stop control-response interval was 26,000ms, followed by validated Wi-Fi with no VPN network agent. All 30 calls succeeded; recomputed median=405ms, nearest-rank P95=588ms, max=725ms. No status counters were captured during that run, so it does not prove per-request shaping or exact impairment values. An earlier attempt in the same continuation lasted 113,102ms; its 30 calls succeeded, but it exceeded 60 seconds and is diagnostic-only. A newer agent-operated Huawei SEA-AL10 run captured 22 Pakomo status polls during the bounded sample window: all reported forwarding/active with active flows; aggregate delayed rose from 66 to 126 while dropped remained 0. The 30 read-only CloudBase application round trips all succeeded (median=393ms, nearest-rank P95=1181ms, max=2048ms). Pakomo stop was confirmed and Wi-Fi validated with no VPN network agent afterward. This status overlap improves run-condition evidence but does not associate counter increments with individual calls or prove exact configured shaping; exact start-to-stop wall-clock duration was not retained, so the fresh 60-second bound cannot be independently reconstructed from timestamps. No database or storage writes occurred. Full transcribed samples, status series and image hashes are in the counter-correlated evidence record.
